The Gateway does gate the memory list: MemoryItemPaginationService.list() calls requireEnabled() (memory-item-pagination-service.ts:21), wired to memoryLifecycleAdminV1Enabled (memory-lifecycle-service.ts:310), which the example config defaults to false, so a new install gets a 409. The UI fix is that describeApiError maps a disabled-feature 409 to category feature_disabled with 'This feature is turned off for this installation.' (describe-api-error.ts:50-52), so stalePage, which needs category conflict, stays false (LibraryMemoryWorkspace.tsx:68) and the false 'changed somewhere else' text is gone. On a default install Library › Memory therefore shows that 'turned off' message in an error callout instead of the memory list, and the callout prints only that summary (LibraryMemoryWorkspace.tsx:200), so it does not say where to turn the setting on. Code read only; the live disabled-flag path was not run (the sandbox has the flag on), and a later task tests it.

note: Promotion claims the candidate with UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'proposed' inside the same transaction that inserts the learning, and rejection uses the same guard, so a second promote or a promote after reject gets a conflict. Code read only; the focused tests were not run.

The learning-created event is published with publication 'deferred' and only sent after the transaction returns (promote and supersede both), so no success event leaves before the commit. Code read only.

Cold-start request count and gzip bytes are production-build measurements; the sandbox is a Vite dev server, so no valid number can be taken and the code does not settle it. To check later: run scripts/verification/lib/scenarios/cockpit-performance-proof.mjs (via its verification lane) against a production build and compare with 20 startup requests and 350,000 initial JS gzip bytes.

Each reader has its own abort (line 252) and the batch fetch is aborted only when every row in it has settled (line 120), so a cancelled reader rejects only itself; fallback direct GETs run per row, once, and only for rows still current and unsettled. Code read only.

Supersession links the predecessor with UPDATE ... WHERE status IN ('proposed','trusted') and inserts the successor in the same transaction; a losing correction sees zero changed rows and throws a conflict before inserting, and its event is published after commit. Code read only.

The receipt check compares spelling aliases of the path (backslashes, ./) and accepts a normalized path; success prints the Gateway's own path and size and clears the submitted draft. Code read; no upload was made in the sandbox.

A real outage needs the Gateway stopped, which this review may not do to the shared sandbox. I tried to emulate it in Chromium by cutting the network for 60 s; the already-open event stream stayed up, so the outage banner never appeared and the test says nothing about it (draft stayed intact). Steps: with the launcher running a Gateway you own, open Chat, type a draft, stop the Gateway process only; expect within ~15 s the banner 'GoatCitadel is unreachable. Sending is paused; your draft is kept.', press Check again and see 'Checking…' then 'Still unreachable · checked <time>', count requests in the Network tab for 30 s (about one probe every 5 s), restart the Gateway and expect the banner to clear without reload and the draft to remain. Chunk failure: block one lazy JS chunk in DevTools and open that area; expect an error with a way to reload.

Needs four hours of wall time, which does not fit this review. Steps: open Chat and an idle Inbox in two tabs on a sandbox, record performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize and the Network request count per minute at 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 hours (DevTools console or a Playwright loop). Pass: heap and requests per minute stay roughly flat with no steady climb.
